rationale: A wins because it mostly keeps the story where the facts can support it, then names the missing proof without decorating the hole. Its line, "Will Skydio name even one utility customer," is the right cold-water question. B has the same basic architecture, but "trade policy created a buyer-side gap" and "right call" turn plausible angles into conclusions the update does not prove.
gaps_in_A: "wildfire-risk mitigation" is an unsupported beat add-on. Power-line inspection can relate to wildfire risk, but the update does not give that peg.

"the first major public proof point since the consumer exit" is overconfident. The facts say Skydio exited consumer drones two years ago and is launching this product now; they do not say this is the first major proof point.
"a live, contracted enterprise product" blurs contract and deployment. The update says contracts with several US utilities, not live deployments.
gaps_in_B: "Space Vacated by Chinese Competitors" is too strong. The update says Chinese drone makers face import restrictions; it does not say they vacated the market.
"trade policy created a buyer-side gap" invents causality. That may be the story, but it needs proof before it appears as framing.
"starting to look like the right call" declares victory without financial proof, named customers, deployment data, or contract values.
"a product in market with paying customers" overstates the facts. The update says Skydio has contracts with several US utilities, not that customers are paying or deployed.
